legend: For an array of integers a$$$a$$$, a triplet of elements is defined by 3 distinct indices (ai,aj,ak)$$$(a_i, a_j, a_k)$$$, and their order does not matter.
Consider the triplets from a$$$a$$$ that sum to zero.
Given an integer k$$$k$$$, construct an array of integers a$$$a$$$ such that exactly k$$$k$$$ triplets of elements from a$$$a$$$ sum to zero.
Your array must have size at most 5000$$$5000$$$.
input: The single line of the input contains an integer k$$$k$$$ (0≤k≤109$$$0 \leq k \leq 10^9$$$) — the required number of triplets that sum to zero.
output: On the first line, output a single integer n$$$n$$$ (0≤n≤5000$$$0 \leq n \leq 5000$$$) — the size of a$$$a$$$.
On the second line, output n$$$n$$$ space-separated integers a1,…,an$$$a_1, \ldots, a_n$$$ (−109≤ai≤109$$$-10^9 \leq a_i \leq 10^9$$$).
If there are multiple arrays satisfying these conditions, output any of them.
It can be shown that a valid answer always exists.
note: In sample 1, no triples in the array a$$$a$$$ sum to zero.
In sample 2, the only triple that sums to zero is (a2,a4,a5)$$$(a_2, a_4, a_5)$$$.
